statement: A bag contains red and blue marbles in the ratio 2 to 5. There are 21 more blue marbles than red ones. How many marbles are in the bag?

choices.misconception: I found the number of red marbles and stopped there.
I gave the difference between blue and red as the total.
I found the number of blue marbles instead of the total.
I multiplied the difference 21 by the 7 parts, as if 21 were the size of one part.

hints: How many parts more does blue have than red?
Treat the ratio as parts. The difference of 21 matches the difference in parts, which tells you the size of one part. Then count all the parts.
Blue has 3 more parts than red, so 3 parts are 21 marbles.

solutions.reliable: Red is 2 parts and blue is 5 parts, so blue has 3 more parts. Those 3 parts are 21 marbles, so one part is 7. The bag holds 7 parts, which is 49 marbles. Check: 14 red and 35 blue differ by 21. The transferable idea: match a known quantity to the right number of parts, find one part, then scale up to whatever the question asks.

whyOnTest: Ratio questions test matching a given quantity to the right number of parts, and then answering the question actually asked.
